newsitem.title: UK: Base metals trade slack, LME pre-market stable.
newsitem.headline: Base metals trade slack, LME pre-market stable.

text.p: Business was patchy during Friday pre-market trading on the LME after a generally uninspiring inventory report, although prices were steady throughout.
Traders said there was little to excite the market so far, although conditions could pick up during the ring sessions with copper perhaps placed to run up and challenge $2,500 again.
Although the pace of warehouse drawdowns has eased - Friday's was a modest 175 tonnes - downside resilience this week and end-week covering may favour the upside today.
Also, the OK Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea will reduce throughput at its mill if it is unable to ship concentrate due to low water levels on the Fly River.
Three months prices were around $2,481/84 a tonne, against Thursday's kerb close of $2,481.
Zinc nudged up to touch a fresh 4-1/2 year high of $1,377 before settling back at an unchanged $1,375. The tone of the market was helped by option interest.
Aluminium was residing just under $1,600, with business at $1,597, down $3. Inventories fell 2,550 tonnes, making the total for the week 16,050 tonnes.
Elsewhere, there was little in the way of significant trading, with markets hardly deviating from Thursday.
Lead was indicated at $640/642 a tonne, up from the previous $638, while tin clawed back above $5,700 to stand at $5,700/5,720. Alloy was quoted at $1,465/75 a tonne.
